mainText:
Fuel excise increases have been delayed by a year, cutting costs for drivers, while ten thousand public servants prepare to strike next week.

New Zealand.

Cabinet has cancelled next year's fuel excise hike, Finance Minister Nicola Willis and Transport Minister Chris Bishop confirmed. Instead the tax rises five cents every six months, starting in twenty twenty eight through to twenty twenty nine. Transport and infrastructure sector bosses say the delay shows political cowardice from both National and Labour, warning it leaves roading projects underfunded.

Around ten thousand public servants will strike from one p.m. on Wednesday the ninth of September, over collective agreement bargaining. It comes as Sir Brian Roche's letter proposes cutting public service agencies from forty two down to as few as fifteen. The union warns the cuts, alongside AI adoption, risk public services.

Business debt has reached one hundred and forty three billion dollars, with three thousand two hundred and seventy five firms entering liquidation over the past year, according to NZ Herald figures. Hospitality is worst hit, with an insolvency rate three point three times the average business. Three thousand hospitality businesses have closed in the past year.

Standard and Poor's has affirmed New Zealand's AA plus credit rating with a stable outlook, forecasting economic growth of two point five percent over the next year. The Reserve Bank's Official Cash Rate decision is due this week, with economists expecting another increase.

In Western Bay of Plenty, Dallas Hohua has had his manslaughter sentence reduced on appeal to as little as two years, for stabbing a friend to death at a party. Councillor Alan Kurtovich says his resignation over the council's Māori wards decision, which triggered a byelection, was the right call despite the cost.

Winston Peters has criticised Christopher Luxon over the Paris climate agreement, as New Zealand First campaigns to leave the deal. Luxon says staying in is non-negotiable in coalition talks, with current coalition partners opposed to the commitment as it stands.

World.

Rescuers in Nepal are using explosives to reach hydropower workers trapped by flooding, with the death toll now at nine hundred and thirty nine. Families continue to wait for word on those missing.

The United States and Iran have traded strikes for the first time in weeks. An attack on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz killed two people and injured two others, the first known US strike since late July.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with residents reporting ongoing gunfire after Congolese troops were overrun. The United Nations estimates more than one million displaced people are now inside the city.

Lionel Messi has retired from international football with Argentina, saying the decision "hurt" but that the time has come. He leaves as his country's most decorated player, following a World Cup win in twenty twenty two.

Technology.

Nvidia's quarterly revenue has doubled to ninety six billion dollars, beating forecasts on continuing demand for AI chips. Separately, Sony and Warner Music are suing AI company Anthropic, alleging it pirated hundreds of song lyrics, including tracks by the Beatles, Taylor Swift and Michael Jackson, to train its models. Anthropic has not yet responded to the claim.

Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey has warned AI could cause a global economic downturn, citing volatility from energy shocks linked to the US Iran conflict. He raised the warning at the G20.

Sport.

Rugby. The All Blacks have won the series decider against the Springboks in Cape Town, treating the third test as the deciding match after Rassie Erasmus and assistant coach Jason Ryan clashed over scrum legality claims through the week.

Rugby, National Provincial Championship. Northland has won the Ranfurly Shield for the first time in fifty years, with Fakatava a standout, and Counties Manukau also on the board this round.

Golf. New Zealander Ryan Fox has made the Presidents Cup International team on form, after missing selection the past two tournaments. Steven Alker has won the Ally Championship in Michigan by three shots, his second straight Champions Tour win.

Netball. Eighteen New Zealand netballers have now left for Australia's domestic league, with the future of the ANZ Premiership uncertain. Netball New Zealand has selected the Mowbray Williams bid to run a new elite domestic competition from twenty twenty seven.

Cricket. Pakistan has dropped seven players and released its head coach after heavy test defeats to England, calling up five uncapped players. A former Black Caps coach has been brought in as part of the overhaul.

Cycling. New Zealander Sammie Maxwell finished fifth at the world cross country mountain bike championships, continuing her comeback after eight months out for wellbeing reasons.

Motorsport. Hayden Paddon finished second at the World Rally Championship's Rally of Paraguay, his best result since his last top level gravel start in twenty eighteen.

Coming up. The Reserve Bank's Official Cash Rate decision is due this week. Public servants strike from one p.m. next Wednesday. Pacific leaders meet in Palau for the Pacific Islands Forum, with Christopher Luxon and Winston Peters attending.

End of flash.
